phys-thermo-01-c1.text: National Institute of Standards and Technology. SI Units – Temperature. NIST.
phys-thermo-01-c1.quote: The kelvin temperature scale begins at absolute zero, the coldest possible temperature
phys-thermo-01-c1.claim: The absolute zero of the kelvin scale (0 K = −273.15 °C) is the lowest possible temperature

phys-thermo-01-c2.text: Rod Nave. Specific Heat. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-01-c2.quote: The specific heat of water is 1 calorie/gram °C = 4.186 joule/gram °C which is higher than any other common substance.
phys-thermo-01-c2.claim: Water has an unusually high specific heat (4,186 J/kg·K)

phys-thermo-02-c1.text: R. Nave. Temperature. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-02-c1.quote: We could say that A is at the same temperature as C even though they are not in contact with each other.
phys-thermo-02-c1.claim: The Zeroth Law formalises the notion of temperature: if A is in thermal equilibrium with B, and B with C, then A and C are also in equilibrium.

phys-thermo-02-c1.text: R. Nave. First Law of Thermodynamics. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-02-c1.quote: The first law of thermodynamics is the application of the conservation of energy principle to heat and thermodynamic processes
phys-thermo-02-c1.claim: The First Law is conservation of energy for thermal systems

phys-thermo-02-c2.text: R. Nave. Second Law of Thermodynamics. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-02-c2.quote: Energy will not flow spontaneously from a low temperature object to a higher temperature object.
phys-thermo-02-c2.claim: Heat flows from hot to cold, not the reverse.

phys-thermo-03-c1.text: Jos Uffink. Philosophy of Statistical Mechanics: Boltzmann. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-thermo-03-c1.quote: The evolution towards equilibrium could then be reformulated as an evolution from less probable to more probable states.
phys-thermo-03-c1.claim: Systems evolve toward high-entropy states simply because there are vastly more of them.

phys-thermo-03-c3.text: Owen Maroney. Information Processing and Thermodynamic Entropy. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-thermo-03-c3.quote: Maxwell's demon was first mentioned in a letter written to Tait in 1867.
phys-thermo-03-c3.claim: Maxwell's Demon, a thought experiment of a tiny creature that could sort fast and slow molecules, seemed to violate the Second Law.

phys-thermo-03-c3.text: Owen Maroney. Information Processing and Thermodynamic Entropy. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-thermo-03-c3.quote: it is not, in fact, measurement but the erasure of the measurement outcome that generates the entropy production in Szilard's example.
phys-thermo-03-c3.claim: The resolution: the demon must store and erase information, and that erasure generates exactly enough entropy to compensate.

phys-thermo-04-c1.text: J. J. O'Connor, E. F. Robertson. Sadi Nicolas Leonard Carnot. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
phys-thermo-04-c1.quote: He showed that the efficiency of the "Carnot engine" depends only on the temperature difference within the engine and not on the substance such as steam that drives the mechanism.
phys-thermo-04-c1.claim: Sadi Carnot proved in 1824 that the maximum possible efficiency depends only on the temperatures of the two reservoirs.

phys-thermo-04-c1.text: R. Nave. Carnot Cycle. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-04-c1.quote: The conceptual value of the Carnot cycle is that it establishes the maximum possible efficiency for an engine cycle operating between T H and T C .
phys-thermo-04-c1.claim: No engine operating between two fixed temperatures can exceed Carnot efficiency

phys-thermo-04-c2.text: R. Nave. Heat Transfer from Cold to Warmer Region. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-04-c2.quote: Refrigerators and heat pumps are examples of heat engines which cause energy to be transferred from a cold area to a hot area.
phys-thermo-04-c2.claim: A refrigerator is a heat engine run in reverse: it uses work to pump heat from a cold interior to a warm room.

phys-thermo-04-c3.text: R. Nave. The Diesel Engine. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-04-c3.quote: The diesel internal combustion engine differs from the gasoline powered Otto cycle by using a higher compression of the fuel to ignite the fuel rather than using a spark plug
phys-thermo-04-c3.claim: Diesel cycle: compression ratio is higher (18:1 vs 8:1), no spark plug

phys-thermo-05-c2.text: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences (1977). The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1977: Press release. NobelPrize.org.
phys-thermo-05-c2.quote: for his contributions to non-equilibrium thermodynamics, particularly the theory of dissipative structures
phys-thermo-05-c2.claim: Ilya Prigogine won the 1977 Nobel Prize for showing that far-from-equilibrium systems can spontaneously self-organise into ordered dissipative structures

phys-thermo-08-c1.text: Owen Maroney. Information Processing and Thermodynamic Entropy. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-thermo-08-c1.quote: Maxwell's demon was first mentioned in a letter written to Tait in 1867.
phys-thermo-08-c1.claim: James Clerk Maxwell imagined (1867) a tiny intelligent being controlling a door between two gas chambers.

phys-thermo-08-c2.text: A. Bérut, A. Petrosyan, S. Ciliberto (2015). Information and thermodynamics: Experimental verification of Landauer's erasure principle. Journal of Statistical Mechanics (arXiv:1503.06537).
phys-thermo-08-c2.quote: We measure the amount of heat dissipated to erase a bit and we establish that in the limit of long erasure cycles the mean dissipated heat saturates at the Landauer bound
phys-thermo-08-c2.claim: The bound has been verified experimentally.

phys-thermo-03-c2.text: Craig Callender. Thermodynamic Asymmetry in Time. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-thermo-03-c2.quote: Although familiar, the thermodynamic arrow of time raises many deep questions relevant to both philosophy and the foundations of physics.
phys-thermo-03-c2.claim: This deep connection between thermodynamics and time is still an active area of research

phys-thermo-05-c1.text: R. B. V. Ferrari, S. B. Soltau (2025). Black Hole Thermodynamics: Established Results, Unresolved Paradoxes, and Speculative Resolutions. arXiv.
phys-thermo-05-c1.quote: Between 1972 and 1975, Jacob Bekenstein proposed that black holes possess entropy proportional to their horizon area, and Stephen Hawking derived this relationship from semiclassical quantum field theory in curved spacetime
phys-thermo-05-c1.claim: In the 1970s, Bekenstein and Hawking discovered that black holes obey laws analogous to thermodynamics.

phys-thermo-06-c1.text: Jos Uffink. Philosophy of Statistical Mechanics: Boltzmann. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phys-thermo-06-c1.quote: That probability distribution was now determined by the size of the volume in phase space corresponding to all the microstates giving rise to the same macrostate
phys-thermo-06-c1.claim: An astronomical number of microstates correspond to any given macrostate

phys-thermo-06-c2.text: R. Nave. Development of Maxwell Distribution. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-06-c2.quote: the probability that any one molecule will be found with energy E decreases exponentially with energy
phys-thermo-06-c2.claim: High-energy states are exponentially suppressed at low T.

phys-thermo-06-c3.text: R. Nave. Specific Heats of Gases. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-06-c3.quote: It took the development of the quantum theory to show that diatomic hydrogen, with its tiny rotational inertia, required a large amount of energy to excite its first excited molecular rotation quantum state.
phys-thermo-06-c3.claim: The departure from classical equipartition was one of the first hints that quantum mechanics was needed.

phys-thermo-07-c1.text: R. Nave. Phase Changes. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-thermo-07-c1.quote: the energies required to accomplish the phase changes (called the latent heat of fusion and latent heat of vaporization ) would lead to plateaus in the temperature vs time graph.
phys-thermo-07-c1.claim: Energy (latent heat) must be added or removed at a specific temperature for the transition to proceed; the temperature pauses while the change happens.

phys-thermo-07-c2.text: Theodore Golfinopoulos (2008). Critical Point. MIT 8.334 course project.
phys-thermo-07-c2.quote: For water, this happens at 374 °C (705 °F) and 218 atmospheres
phys-thermo-07-c2.claim: Approach the critical point of water (374 °C, 218 atm) and the distinction between liquid and gas vanishes
